paragraphs.text: I charge [thee] in the sight of God, and of Christ Jesus, who shall judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom:
paragraphs.original: Διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, τοῦ μέλλοντος κρίνειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, καὶ τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Diamartyromai enōpion tou theou kai Christou Iēsou, tou mellontos krinein zōntas kai nekrous, kai tēn epiphaneian autou kai tēn basileian autou·

paragraphs.text: preach the word; be urgent in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all longsuffering and teaching.
paragraphs.original: κήρυξον τὸν λόγον, ἐπίστηθι εὐκαίρως ἀκαίρως, ἔλεγξον, ἐπιτίμησον, παρακάλεσον, ἐν πάσῃ μακροθυμίᾳ καὶ διδαχῇ.
paragraphs.translit: kēryxon ton logon, epistēthi eukairōs akairōs, elenxon, epitimēson, parakaleson, en pasē makrothymia kai didachē.

paragraphs.text: For the time will come when they will not endure the sound doctrine; but, having itching ears, will heap to themselves teachers after their own lusts;
paragraphs.original: ἔσται γὰρ καιρὸς ὅτε τῆς ὑγιαινούσης διδασκαλίας οὐκ ἀνέξονται, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισωρεύσουσιν διδασκάλους κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν,
paragraphs.translit: estai gar kairos hote tēs hygiainousēs didaskalias ouk anexontai, alla kata tas idias epithymias heautois episōreusousin didaskalous knēthomenoi tēn akoēn,

paragraphs.text: and will turn away their ears from the truth, and turn aside unto fables.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπὸ μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσιν, ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μύθους ἐκτραπήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: kai apo men tēs alētheias tēn akoēn apostrepsousin, epi de tous mythous ektrapēsontai.

paragraphs.text: But be thou sober in all things, suffer hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfil thy ministry.
paragraphs.original: σὺ δὲ νῆφε ἐν πᾶσιν, κακοπάθησον, ἔργον ποίησον εὐαγγελιστοῦ, τὴν διακονίαν σου πληροφόρησον.
paragraphs.translit: sy de nēphe en pasin, kakopathēson, ergon poiēson euangelistou, tēn diakonian sou plērophorēson.

paragraphs.text: For I am already being offered, and the time of my departure is come.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγὼ γὰρ ἤδη σπένδομαι, καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῆς ἀναλύσεώς μου ἐφέστηκεν.
paragraphs.translit: Egō gar ēdē spendomai, kai ho kairos tēs analyseōs mou ephestēken.

paragraphs.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith:
paragraphs.original: τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα ἠγώνισμαι, τὸν δρόμον τετέλεκα, τὴν πίστιν τετήρηκα·
paragraphs.translit: ton kalon agōna ēgōnismai, ton dromon teteleka, tēn pistin tetērēka·

paragraphs.text: henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give to me at that day; and not to me only, but also to all them that have loved his appearing.
paragraphs.original: λοιπὸν ἀπόκειταί μοι ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης στέφανος, ὃν ἀποδώσει μοι ὁ κύριος ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, ὁ δίκαιος κριτής, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐμοὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἠγαπηκόσι τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: loipon apokeitai moi ho tēs dikaiosynēs stephanos, hon apodōsei moi ho kyrios en ekeinē tē hēmera, ho dikaios kritēs, ou monon de emoi alla kai pasin tois ēgapēkosi tēn epiphaneian autou.

paragraphs.text: Give diligence to come shortly unto me:
paragraphs.original: Σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με ταχέως·
paragraphs.translit: Spoudason elthein pros me tacheōs·

paragraphs.text: for Demas forsook me, having loved this present world, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
paragraphs.original: Δημᾶς γάρ με ἐγκατέλιπεν ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα, καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, Κρήσκης εἰς Γαλατίαν, Τίτος εἰς Δαλματίαν·
paragraphs.translit: Dēmas gar me enkatelipen agapēsas ton nyn aiōna, kai eporeuthē eis Thessalonikēn, Krēskēs eis Galatian, Titos eis Dalmatian·

paragraphs.text: Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee; for he is useful to me for ministering.
paragraphs.original: Λουκᾶς ἐστιν μόνος μετʼ ἐμοῦ. Μᾶρκον ἀναλαβὼν ἄγε μετὰ σεαυτοῦ, ἔστιν γάρ μοι εὔχρηστος εἰς διακονίαν,
paragraphs.translit: Loukas estin monos metʼ emou. Markon analabōn age meta seautou, estin gar moi euchrēstos eis diakonian,

paragraphs.text: But Tychicus I sent to Ephesus.
paragraphs.original: Τυχικὸν δὲ ἀπέστειλα εἰς Ἔφεσον.
paragraphs.translit: Tychikon de apesteila eis Epheson.

paragraphs.text: The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, bring when thou comest, and the books, especially the parchments.
paragraphs.original: τὸν φαιλόνην, ὃν ἀπέλιπον ἐν Τρῳάδι παρὰ Κάρπῳ, ἐρχόμενος φέρε, καὶ τὰ βιβλία, μάλιστα τὰς μεμβράνας.
paragraphs.translit: ton phailonēn, hon apelipon en Trōadi para Karpō, erchomenos phere, kai ta biblia, malista tas membranas.

paragraphs.text: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord will render to him according to his works:
paragraphs.original: Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ χαλκεὺς πολλά μοι κακὰ ἐνεδείξατο— ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ—
paragraphs.translit: Alexandros ho chalkeus polla moi kaka enedeixato— apodōsei autō ho kyrios kata ta erga autou—

paragraphs.text: of whom do thou also beware; for he greatly withstood our words.
paragraphs.original: ὃν καὶ σὺ φυλάσσου, λίαν γὰρ ἀντέστη τοῖς ἡμετέροις λόγοις.
paragraphs.translit: hon kai sy phylassou, lian gar antestē tois hēmeterois logois.

paragraphs.text: At my first defence no one took my part, but all forsook me: may it not be laid to their account.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ μου ἀπολογίᾳ οὐδείς μοι παρεγένετο, ἀλλὰ πάντες με ἐγκατέλιπον— μὴ αὐτοῖς λογισθείη—
paragraphs.translit: En tē prōtē mou apologia oudeis moi paregeneto, alla pantes me enkatelipon— mē autois logistheiē—

paragraphs.text: But the Lord stood by me, and strengthened me; that through me the message might me fully proclaimed, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ κύριός μοι παρέστη καὶ ἐνεδυνάμωσέν με, ἵνα διʼ ἐμοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα πληροφορηθῇ καὶ ἀκούσωσιν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐρρύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος.
paragraphs.translit: ho de kyrios moi parestē kai enedynamōsen me, hina diʼ emou to kērygma plērophorēthē kai akousōsin panta ta ethnē, kai errysthēn ek stomatos leontos.

paragraphs.text: The Lord will deliver me from every evil work, and will save me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom [be] the glory forever and ever. Amen.
paragraphs.original: ῥύσεταί με ὁ κύριος ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔργου πονηροῦ καὶ σώσει εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐπουράνιον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.
paragraphs.translit: rhysetai me ho kyrios apo pantos ergou ponērou kai sōsei eis tēn basileian autou tēn epouranion· hō hē doxa eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn, amēn.

paragraphs.text: Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the house of Onesiphorus.
paragraphs.original: Ἄσπασαι Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν καὶ τὸν Ὀνησιφόρου οἶκον.
paragraphs.translit: Aspasai Priskan kai Akylan kai ton Onēsiphorou oikon.

paragraphs.text: Erastus remained at Corinth: but Trophimus I left at Miletus sick.
paragraphs.original: Ἔραστος ἔμεινεν ἐν Κορίνθῳ, Τρόφιμον δὲ ἀπέλιπον ἐν Μιλήτῳ ἀσθενοῦντα.
paragraphs.translit: Erastos emeinen en Korinthō, Trophimon de apelipon en Milētō asthenounta.

paragraphs.text: Give diligence to come before winter. Eubulus saluteth thee, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren.
paragraphs.original: Σπούδασον πρὸ χειμῶνος ἐλθεῖν. Ἀσπάζεταί σε Εὔβουλος καὶ Πούδης καὶ Λίνος καὶ Κλαυδία καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες.
paragraphs.translit: Spoudason pro cheimōnos elthein. Aspazetai se Euboulos kai Poudēs kai Linos kai Klaudia kai hoi adelphoi pantes.

paragraphs.text: The Lord be with thy spirit. Grace be with you.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ κύριος μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματός σου. ἡ χάρις μεθʼ ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Ho kyrios meta tou pneumatos sou. hē charis methʼ hymōn.
